items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: We made that thing, man, and we made jokes out of everything... Simeon's the lead alto player.

ctx.x: That was the greatest teacher, you know. So he said, 'Is that me? Man, that can't be.' I said, 'Well, listen to the notes, Willie.' I said, 'That's you. That

Simeon. " Simeon's isn't Simeon. Simeon's the lead alto player. He says, "Now I hear, I see how bad I sounded." It was fun. We made that thing, man, and we made jokes out of everything. Nobody got mad, you know, but it was a constructive criticism, you know, so it worked out real fine. And I got so I could get that mellowness that I wanted, you know, in the section.

When we were talking the other day, you had said that in the beginning everything that you played was written out -- piano parts were generally written out. By this time again, 19 -- mid-thirties, were pianists still having everything written out? I mean on the stock arrangements, we do see them written, but what about your own arrangements?
